issues.legal_issue: The State must provide compensation for deaths and injuries caused by police firing without limiting the payment to some victims or treating it as extinguishing the wrongdoer’s liability.
material_facts: The State did not dispute that police firing caused deaths and injuries.
Compensation had been paid to the relations of only a few deceased persons, and no justification was given for withholding compensation in other cases.
The State stated that it did not intend to deprive the remaining victims’ relations of compensation.
issues.conclusion: The State was directed to pay compensation for every death and every injured person, adjusting any compensation already paid. The direction was without prejudice to further just claims, and payment did not absolve the wrongdoer of liability.
issues.legal_principle: In a proceeding under Article 32 of the Constitution, the Court treated State compensation following deaths or injuries in police firing as a normal practice and directed payment on a consistent basis. The payment was a working principle intended to assist the dependants of the deceased; it did not extinguish the wrongdoer’s liability or prejudice further just compensation claims. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: constitutional_writ_proceeding and (death_caused_by_police_firing or injury_caused_by_police_firing) and state_compensation_is_customary and compensation_withheld_from_some_victims_without_justification

predicates.constitutional_writ_proceeding: The matter is brought as a constitutional writ proceeding.
predicates.death_caused_by_police_firing: Police firing caused one or more deaths.
predicates.injury_caused_by_police_firing: Police firing caused one or more injuries.
predicates.state_compensation_is_customary: The State ordinarily provides compensation when police firing causes deaths or injuries.
predicates.compensation_withheld_from_some_victims_: The State has compensated some victims but has not justified withholding compensation from others.

issues.definition: When a constitutional writ proceeding concerns deaths or injuries caused by police firing and customary State compensation has been withheld from some victims without justification, the State must compensate each death and injury without extinguishing further claims.

issues.legal_issue: A pending proceeding in a lower court should not be transferred when that court is better placed to gather relevant material and transfer would occur without notice and a reasonable opportunity for affected parties.
material_facts: A related writ petition was already pending in the High Court.
The High Court was closer to the parties and better placed to obtain documents and, if necessary, affidavits.
The Court considered that transfer without notice and a reasonable opportunity for the parties in the pending petition would be inappropriate.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to transfer the pending writ petition and left the petitioner free to seek impleadment in it or file a separate application before the High Court.
issues.legal_principle: In disposing of a proceeding under Article 32, the Court considered the practical advantages of the High Court’s proximity and ability to obtain material, as well as the need to give affected parties notice and a reasonable opportunity before transfer. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.constitutional_writ_proceeding: The matter is brought as a constitutional writ proceeding.
predicates.related_lower_court_case_pending: A related case is already pending in a lower court.
predicates.lower_court_has_proximity_and_fact_gathe: The lower court is better placed by proximity or procedure to obtain relevant material from the parties.
predicates.transfer_would_occur_without_notice_or_r: The proposed transfer would be made without notice and a reasonable opportunity for affected parties.

issues.definition: When a related lower-court case is pending and that court is better placed to gather material, a transfer that would deny affected parties notice and a reasonable opportunity should be declined, while allowing the petitioner to participate there or proceed separately.

issues.legal_issue: The High Court should decide whether a report subject to a claim of privilege should be disclosed when disclosure is pressed in a proceeding before it.
material_facts: A State inquiry had produced a report, and the State had claimed privilege against its disclosure.
The Court left open whether the report should be made public and whether the privilege claim should be upheld.
The petitioner could seek disclosure after joining the pending High Court proceeding or filing a separate application.
issues.conclusion: If the petitioner joined the pending High Court proceeding or filed a separate application and pressed for disclosure, the High Court could examine whether the report should be made public and, if privilege was claimed, decide the privilege question.
issues.legal_principle: The Court left the disclosure and privilege questions for examination by the High Court in the proceeding brought before it. No specific provision or earlier case was relied on for this direction.

predicates.related_high_court_proceeding_available: A related proceeding is pending before, or may be brought before, the High Court.
predicates.petitioner_seeks_disclosure_of_inquiry_r: The petitioner asks the High Court to make an inquiry report public.
predicates.privilege_claimed_over_report: A party claims that the inquiry report is protected from disclosure.

issues.definition: When a petitioner seeks disclosure of a report in a related High Court proceeding and privilege is claimed, the High Court may decide both disclosure and the privilege claim.

issues.legal_issue: A pending police investigation should be completed within the period directed by the Court, while an aggrieved person may challenge the maintainability of charges if a charge sheet is submitted.
material_facts: A police case arising from the incident remained under investigation.
The petitioner alleged that the case falsely implicated innocent people, but the factual assertions were disputed.

The Court directed completion of the investigation within three months and preserved the ability of the petitioner or another aggrieved person to challenge the maintainability of charges if a charge sheet was submitted.
issues.conclusion: The investigation was directed to be completed within three months. If a charge sheet was submitted, the petitioner or any other aggrieved party could challenge the maintainability of the charges in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: The Court directed completion of the pending investigation within a specified period and left any challenge to the maintainability of charges to be made in accordance with law if a charge sheet was submitted. No specific provision or earlier case was relied on for this direction.

predicates.police_investigation_pending: A police investigation concerning the matter remains unfinished.
predicates.proceeding_seeks_court_relief_concerning: A proceeding asks the Court to address the pending investigation.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns an unfinished police investigation, the investigation must be completed within the period directed by the Court, and aggrieved persons may challenge charges submitted afterward.

issues.legal_issue: A report that does not bear on the issues requiring resolution need not be called for by the lower court and may be returned to the authority from which it came.
material_facts: A report by an Assistant Commissioner concerning scheduled castes and scheduled tribes had been produced at the petitioner’s instance.
The Court read the report and found it irrelevant to the point in issue.
issues.conclusion: The Court directed that the report need not be called for by the High Court and be returned to the appropriate Ministry.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the report’s lack of relevance to the issues as a reason not to require it in the pending High Court proceeding and directed its return. No specific provision or earlier case was relied on.

predicates.report_produced_in_court: A report has been produced before the Court.
predicates.report_does_not_address_an_issue_requiri: The report does not bear on an issue that the Court needs to resolve.

issues.definition: When a report produced before the Court does not address an issue requiring resolution, it need not be called for in the related proceeding and should be returned.
